title: Command to verify quadlet files
body:
### Feature request description

I'm running a lot of quadlets on my homelab and recently discovered one of them wasn't being run. I could see it picked up in `podman quadlet list` but had a status of `Not loaded`. Checking the file itself I didn't see anything wrong with it and was clueless until I found `/usr/lib/systemd/system-generators/podman-system-generator` which told me what the error was - I had renamed a volume a while back and not updated it here.

It isn't obvious why a quadlet isn't loaded nor is it easy to know if it is an issue in the file or somewhere else using the commands available through `podman`

### Suggest potential solution

Expose a new command `podman quadlet verify` or `podman quadlet info <name>`

### Have you considered any alternatives?

Can run `/usr/lib/systemd/system-generators/podman-system-generator --dryrun` to get information

### Additional context

_No response_

Hi @Honny1  and @Venefilyn ,

I investigated the current Quadlet CLI and generator behavior to understand where "Not loaded" comes from and how "quadlet verify" could fit in.

### Current behavior

podman quadlet list` discovers Quadlet files, parses them, derives the corresponding systemd unit name, and checks the unit state through systemd. When the generated unit is not available/loaded, the CLI reports Not loaded.

However, this path does not run the full Quadlet conversion performed by the generator, so it cannot always expose the underlying conversion/validation error.

I also tested the existing generator with an intentionally invalid `.container` file. Running:
quadlet --dryrun
runs the actual conversion logic and reports errors such as:
converting "broken.container": no Image or Rootfs key specified
processing encountered some errors
and exits with a non-zero status.

### Proposed design
I propose adding:
podman quadlet verify
The command would validate Quadlet files using the same conversion/validation path used by the Quadlet generator, rather than implementing a second set of validation rules in the Podman CLI.

For example:
$ podman quadlet verify

broken.container:
  error: no Image or Rootfs key specified

valid.container:
  OK

The command should return a non-zero exit status when one or more Quadlets fail validation.

### Implementation consideration

There appear to be two possible approaches:

1. Reuse the existing Quadlet generator/dry-run functionality directly.
2. Refactor the reusable generation/validation logic into the existing Quadlet package so both the generator and `podman quadlet verify` can use it without duplicating logic.

I currently lean toward sharing the existing conversion logic rather than duplicating validation in the CLI, but I would like feedback from maintainers on which approach fits the project architecture better.

### Testing

I would add tests covering:

* valid Quadlet files
* invalid Quadlet files and useful conversion errors
* multiple Quadlet files where some pass and some fail
* correct exit status
* the supported Quadlet types where applicable

I have not started implementation yet, so I would appreciate feedback on the proposed behavior and architecture before proceeding.
